comparisons.peer_topic: Accounting measurement and fee recognition for loans
comparisons.peer_summary: Loans are reported at outstanding principal net of unearned income, charge-offs, and deferred fees, with origination fees and direct costs deferred and recognized over the loan life using a constant effective yield methodology.
comparisons.comparison: Both C and BAC disclose that consumer/loan balances are net of unearned income, primarily consisting of deferred loan origination fees that are recognized as interest income over the life of the related loans. Specifically, C notes unearned income of $889 million (2024) and $802 million (2023) primarily representing deferred loan origination fees, while BAC states loans are reported net of unearned income, deferred fees and costs which are deferred and recognized as adjustments to interest income over the lives of the related loans.

sentences.text: (11)Consumer loans were net of unearned income of $889 million and $802 million at December 31, 2024 and 2023, respectively.

Unearned income on consumer loans primarily represents loan origination fees, net of certain direct origination costs, that are deferred and recognized as Interest income over the lives of the related loans.

Loans, with the exception of loans accounted for under the fair value option, are reported at their outstanding principal balances net of any unearned income, charge-offs, unamortized deferred fees and costs on originated loans, and for purchased loans, net of any unamortized premiums or discounts.
Loan origination fees and certain direct origination costs are deferred and recognized as adjustments to interest income over the lives of the related loans.

comparisons.peer_topic: Interest income recognition for performing loans
comparisons.peer_summary: Interest income on performing loans held-for-investment is recognized at the contractual rate, with purchase price discounts or premiums and net deferred loan fees or costs amortized over the contractual life as a yield adjustment.
comparisons.comparison: Both C and JPM disclose the treatment of deferred loan fees/costs as adjustments to interest income over the loan life. C states unearned income (primarily deferred loan origination fees) is recognized as interest income over the lives of the loans. JPM states that purchase price discounts or premiums, as well as net deferred loan fees or costs, are recognized in interest income over the contractual life of the loan as an adjustment of yield.
